feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital/public-sector communications roles: the experience progression is clear, the scope is substantial, and the technical + leadership blend is compelling. Writing is generally polished, but the document is slightly repetitive and would be stronger with tighter structure, more quantified outcomes, and a few style/grammar fixes.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior positioning: the headline, summary, and career progression at NACo strongly support leadership credibility.  
- Good evidence of scale and complexity: 10,000+ page migration, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers, analytics stack, and studio build-out add impact.  
- Broad but relevant skill mix: strategy, governance, Drupal/CMS delivery, analytics, multimedia, and AI-enabled search are well aligned.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication across Core Competencies, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT; consolidate to improve scannability and avoid repetition.  
- Add more outcome-focused metrics beyond activity/scope: e.g., engagement growth, efficiency gains, adoption rates, campaign performance, or cost savings.  
- Fix minor style/grammar inconsistencies: “social, and multimedia” should be “social and multimedia”; “12+ years of experience” slightly conflicts with 2013–present timeline; punctuation/bullet formatting is inconsistent, and “A2/Learning” reads awkwardly—use “A2 (learning).”
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear seniority and domain focus. It reads well, but it’s slightly broad and repeats themes covered in the subtitle, competencies, and work experience.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Make it more outcome-oriented by anchoring the scope in enterprise/public-sector scale rather than listing functions.
- Tighten the service list to the most differentiating strengths: web modernization, governance/editorial systems, analytics, and AI-enabled discovery.
- Replace “Leads” with a first-person implied value statement that reads more like a headline summary.
- Suggested rewrite: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing enterprise web platforms, governance models, and content operations for high-volume public-sector organizations. Combines digital strategy, editorial systems, analytics infrastructure, multimedia operations, and AI-enabled search/content experiences to improve how mission-driven institutions publish, govern, and scale communications.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with recent projects and skills; “AI-enabled search/content experiences” is more specific.
- “Platforms, governance models and content operations” closely echoes Core Competencies; avoid adding more functional lists here.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block largely repeats the header and Topline Skills. It would be more effective if tightened, made more distinctive, and aligned to the most senior/recent value areas.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, leadership-level wording: “Enterprise web modernization,” “Digital governance and editorial operations,” “Analytics, dashboards and reporting systems.”
- Prioritize the strongest recent differentiators: AI-enabled search, workflow automation/integrations, and public-sector communications.
- Standardize style by avoiding mixed constructions like “operations,” “systems,” and “experiences” unless intentionally parallel.
- Suggested rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, dashboards and reporting systems • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integrations • Public-sector and advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multi-channel communications operations” overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills; consider dropping it.
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” is already well covered in Topline Skills and work experience.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshots, but the block repeats themes already covered in Work Experience and Core Competencies. It will be stronger if tightened, made more parallel in style, and focused on distinctive outcomes or formats not stated elsewhere.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and format each item consistently with action + platform + purpose.
- Tighten phrasing: “hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search, and bill-level AI chat” and “10'×20' interactive conference display.”
- Emphasize what is unique in each project: legislative discovery, Drupal 10 campaign architecture, integrated anniversary storytelling, recurring advocacy video operations.
- Consider shortening to 2–3 highest-value projects if space is tight, prioritizing the AI search and Drupal microsite as most recent/relevant.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite development, and advocacy video series substantially overlap with the current freelance and NACo experience bullets.
- “Built/Developed” repeats throughout; vary verbs or use a cleaner noun-led project format.

Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Core Competencies

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical range, but it reads broad and overlaps with your NACo entries. Tighten it around what is new, senior, and distinctive here—especially consulting scope, enterprise improvement, and AI-enabled search.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + client context: “Serve as strategic communications consultant to a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital strategy, web operations, and platform improvement initiatives.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into sharper outcome-oriented lines: “Built cross-functional workflows, analytics, and governance systems to improve coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Make the Drupal/CMS bullet more concise: “Designed and launched Drupal-based campaign experiences, including microsites, modular content components, and member-facing resource toolkits.”
- Elevate the most distinctive item: “Led an AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval strategy, structured content requirements, and user-facing discovery experience.” Add metrics if possible (adoption, efficiency, search success, launch timeline).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” strongly repeats NACo; keep only if you can show a different scale, client context, or result.
- “CMS development/front-end implementation” may duplicate skills sections; focus on business impact, not task list.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management and video points covered in earlier NACo roles and recent projects.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope/outcome summary: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Recast bullets to foreground impact: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable results where missing: growth in email engagement, social reach, production cost/time savings from the studio, reporting efficiency gains, or governance adoption/compliance metrics.
- Tighten phrasing by removing softer language like “helping,” “expanding,” and “improving” unless paired with a concrete result.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this at a higher strategic/organizational level.
- Video studio/buildout overlaps with footer projects and earlier NACo video bullets; focus on operational/business impact, not production activity.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story and good scope, but this entry overlaps with the later NACo director role and earlier manager role. Make it more distinct by emphasizing executional leadership, channel growth, and concrete outputs before the strategic/platform modernization work in the next role.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper scope/result line: “Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social, and video, coordinating advocacy and editorial publishing for NACo’s core member audiences.”
- Tighten bullets to focus on distinct contributions:
- Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Built cross-team editorial planning processes across communications, advocacy, and program staff to improve alignment and publishing cadence.
- Standardized digital publishing workflows to improve consistency, speed, and coordination across channels.
- If possible, add metrics: email open/click rates, video views, publishing volume, turnaround-time improvements, or audience growth.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Strengthened editorial planning” and “improved publishing workflows” overlap with the 2022–2024 role’s governance/planning language.
- Weekly video updates are also mentioned in the 2015–2018 role; clarify this entry as scaling/formalizing the program.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning

Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline item overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo bullets. Make it sharper, more senior, and more differentiated from the technical skills section.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe toward leadership scope and outcomes, not generic capability labels.
- Tighten phrasing and reduce overlap with “Core Competencies” and work history.
- Suggested rewrite:
- Enterprise digital strategy and platform modernization
- Editorial governance and scalable content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership across web, email, social and video
- Public-sector, membership and advocacy communications
- Audience-centered content strategy, planning and messaging
- If space allows, replace one bullet with a stronger impact-oriented phrase such as “Digital transformation for complex, mission-driven organizations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Multi-channel communications leadership” repeat the header/Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Audience-focused content planning” is weaker and less distinctive than your governance/operations strengths shown in recent roles.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution

Suggested edit:

- Front-end web implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery)

Suggested edit

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production

Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies plus multiple NACo bullets. Make it more senior, specific, and aligned to recent leadership-level delivery.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Multimedia Production, Studio Operations & Event Delivery**

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” section. This item should either be tightened to avoid repetition or reframed to emphasize depth in the most relevant platforms, especially Drupal.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with: Drupal (enterprise content architecture, migration, modular microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Microsoft Power Pages • GitHub Pages
- Put Drupal first and add a brief qualifier to reflect recent, high-impact work without turning this into a full sentence.
- Standardize naming: use “Microsoft Power Pages” instead of “Power Pages” for clarity/searchability.
- If space is tight, consider dropping GitHub Pages unless it is used meaningfully in recent work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely repeats “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already includes Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, and Power Pages.
- Avoid listing the same platforms in multiple sections unless this version adds specificity (e.g., enterprise Drupal focus).

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should feel more implementation-focused and current, with cleaner grouping.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery
- Add clearer technical grouping: Integrations & deployment: API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions
- If accurate, replace older/general terms with stronger specifics tied to recent work, e.g., “custom Drupal front-end implementation,” “tag deployment,” or “serverless scripting”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) for a more modern, concise style unless used consistently elsewhere

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills; keep one section broader and this one more tool-specific
- “GitHub Actions” may fit better under “Automation & Workflow Systems” unless you want this section strictly focused on technical delivery

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems expertise. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already called out in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a pure list to grouped, purpose-led categories: “Workflow automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier; Project/issue tracking: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp; Collaboration: Slack, Teams.”
- If space allows, add a light qualifier tied to recent work, e.g. “used to support editorial planning, cross-team coordination, and communications operations.”
- Prioritize the strongest, most relevant tools first; consider dropping older/generic collaboration tools if they’re not central.
- Keep naming consistent with the rest of the CV; use either “Power Automate” or “Microsoft Power Automate” depending on other Microsoft product references.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills, so avoid repeating those exact phrases here.
- Slack and Teams are common workplace tools; listing both may add little unless collaboration platforms are specifically important to the target role.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The item is clear but too bare to add much value on its own. Since email leadership already appears in recent roles, this line should stay concise and emphasize platform breadth rather than repeat channel ownership.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms
- Tighten platform naming for readability and ATS match: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights/Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If accurate, add one qualifier to show level of use without duplicating experience bullets, e.g. “administration, campaign deployment, and audience segmentation”
- Keep it as a platform list only unless you can support a measurable outcome elsewhere; this section should signal tools, not restate responsibilities

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding “newsletters,” “email strategy,” or audience-size claims here; those are already covered in the NACo experience entries
- Don’t expand into analytics or automation tools in this item; those are already captured under separate Technical + IT categories

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization” and the NACo Director role. Use it to sharpen the technical stack, not restate capabilities.

Suggested edit:
- Tighten to platform-first phrasing: “GA4 • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console • A/B testing • KPI dashboards”
- Replace broad terms like “SEO” and “Dashboarding” with more specific, resume-friendly labels such as “technical SEO / search performance” and “KPI dashboards / executive reporting”
- If accurate, add one higher-signal tool already implied by your work, e.g., “Google Search Console” or “tagging/measurement strategy” rather than generic optimization language
- Keep this as a pure tools/methods line; let impact stay in recent roles where you already mention analytics infrastructure expansion

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Near-duplicate of “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization”; consider trimming one or making this strictly tools while the other stays capability-focused
- “Dashboarding” repeats “reporting infrastructure” language from Core Competencies and Work Experience

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression signal, but the item is too general and overlaps with the stronger 2018–2024 NACo entries. Make this role clearly foundational: team-building, early platform/content execution, and first-line supervision.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize progression and firsts: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital media function supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations.”
- Add clearer ownership and outcomes where possible: “Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates, to expand member-facing communications.”
- Tighten the management point: “Provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate and helped formalize early publishing and production workflows.”
- If you have metrics, add them: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, email/social engagement, or workflow/time savings.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 advocacy video bullet; differentiate this as the earlier launch/build phase.
- Avoid repeating broad “strengthened workflows” language already used in later NACo roles unless you specify what changed.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads broadly and undersells the strongest differentiator: launching NACo’s first podcast. Since later roles already cover digital/media leadership, this item should emphasize foundational innovation, research support, and first-of-its-kind multimedia work.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the standout achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county-focused programs and policy priorities, while expanding NACo’s early digital content capabilities.”
- Add a sharper second sentence: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials” with specifics if available: videos, web features, interviews, or stakeholder-facing resources.
- If possible, add scope or outcome: number of episodes, audiences served, internal teams supported, or how the podcast/content supported advocacy or member engagement.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating generic “digital content production” language already covered more strongly in later NACo roles.
- Don’t overemphasize video/multimedia leadership here if those accomplishments are better established in 2015–2024 roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills list, but it reads more like a mixed capabilities bucket than a clean tools section. It also overlaps with stronger, more recent multimedia leadership already shown in work experience and Topline Skills.

Suggested edit
- Rename or tighten to emphasize software/tools only: “Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator”
- If you want to keep production capabilities, split them from tools: “Video/audio editing • Livestream studio operations • Podcast production”
- Consider a sharper rewrite: “Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator • Livestream studio operations • Podcast production”
